Let me execute all phases of the planning protocol: 1. **Scope & Context** - Understand what's being built 2. **Semantic Structure Plan** - HTML structure and landmarks 3. **Interaction Pattern Design** - Map to APG patterns, keyboard model 4. **Focus Management Plan** - Tab order, focus traps, restoration 5. **State Communication Design** - How states are communicated 6. **Visual Accessibility Plan** - Color contrast, touch targets, etc. 7. **Content Accessibility Plan** - Labels, link text, error messages 8. **Testing Strategy** - Automated and manual testing plans 9. **Implementation Tasks & Review Checkpoints** - Breakdown into tasks Let me plan this carefully based on the APG Menu Button pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/). Key design decisions: - The button uses `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` to indicate state - The dropdown menu uses `role="menu"` - Each item uses `role="menuitem"` - Disabled items use `aria-disabled="true"` (not the native disabled attribute since they're not real form controls) - Keyboard model: Tab to button, Enter/Space to open, Arrow Down/Up to navigate, Enter to select, Escape to close - Focus management: When menu opens, focus moves to first item OR stays on button. Per APG pattern, focus should move to the first menuitem when opened via keyboard (Enter/Space), but stay on button if opened via mouse click. Actually, let me reconsider - the APG pattern says focus moves to the next/selected item in the menu. - Focus restoration: When menu closes, focus returns to the button Let me write a comprehensive plan following all 9 phases of the protocol.# Menu Button with Dropdown Accessibility Design Plan > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users (JAWS, NVDA), keyboard-only users, low vision users > **Assistive technologies:** JAWS, NVDA, keyboard-only navigation **Feature:** A reusable React menu button component that opens a dropdown list of selectable items with full keyboard support and screen reader compatibility. **Risk Level:** Medium — Composite widget with dynamic content, focus management across open/close states, disabled item handling, and potential nested submenus. **Component/Page Type:** Menu Button (APG pattern), Dropdown Menu, Interactive Widget --- ## Scope & Context ### What is being built A reusable React `MenuButton` component that renders a button labeled "Menu" or "Actions". Clicking the button opens a dropdown panel containing 5-8 selectable menu items. Users can select items via mouse click or keyboard navigation. The Escape key closes the open menu. Some items may be disabled, and nested submenus are an optional future enhancement. ### User needs Users need to access a set of actions from a compact button interface. Screen reader users need to understand when the menu is expanded/collapsed and navigate items efficiently. Keyboard-only users need full keyboard control without getting trapped or losing focus context. Low vision users need clear visual focus indicators and sufficient color contrast. ### Compliance target WCAG 2.2 AA — all Level A and Level AA success criteria must be satisfied. ### Assistive technologies to support - **JAWS** (Windows) — screen reader with virtual cursor and forms mode - **NVDA** (Windows, free) — screen reader with browse and focus modes - **Keyboard-only users** — Tab navigation, arrow keys, Enter/Space/Escape - Focus on Windows-based screen readers since the platform is a React web application ### Risk factors 1. **Focus management complexity**: Deciding where focus goes when menu opens (button vs first item) and ensuring proper restoration on close 2. **Dynamic content rendering**: Menu items rendered conditionally — must ensure ARIA states update correctly 3. **Disabled item handling**: Disabled items must be in the tab order context but not activatable, with correct screen reader announcements 4. **Composite widget keyboard model**: Arrow key navigation within menu requires roving tabindex implementation 5. **Nested submenu potential**: Optional submenus add complexity to focus management and escape behavior ### Constraints - React application (hooks-based component) - No existing code — greenfield component - Must be reusable across the application - Some items may be disabled via a `disabled` prop on individual menu item data - Nested submenus are optional but should not break core functionality if added later --- ## Semantic Structure Plan ### Document structure and landmarks The MenuButton is an inline widget, not a full page. It does not introduce new landmark regions itself — it lives within the existing page's main content or navigation area. The component consists of: - A trigger button (the menu button) - A dropdown panel containing menu items No additional `
`, `
`, or other landmarks are needed for this widget alone. ### Heading hierarchy The MenuButton does not introduce headings. If the dropdown contains grouped actions, those could optionally use `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="horizontal"` to visually and semantically group related items (per APG Menu pattern). No heading elements should be used inside a menu button dropdown unless it's a complex mega-menu — for this moderate-complexity component, headings are not needed. ### Structure diagram ```html
